primary_citations.passage:
Some effects remove Invaders, representing them fleeing in terror. Return the specified pieces to the 
supply. Some replace Invaders: first you remove the Invader, then you put something else in its place. 
A replaced Invader keeps any Damage it had. More Powers destroy Invaders outright. Return the 
specified pieces to the supply. Destroying a Town generates 1 Fear and destroying a City generates 2 
Fear, but removing or replacing does not.

changed_material.description: Drowning paragraph now explicitly assigns the survivor Push to the failed Drowning action and applies non-moving cleanup directly only after the action tree. The inaccurate cross-reference to a cleanup procedure below was removed. Net +135 characters.
changed_material.assessment: Accurate. Same-action Push may trigger further actions; all actions finish before post-tree cleanup and the outcome check. The post-tree correction itself causes no Push, move, remove, destruction or triggered action. Failure gives Ocean no Energy. Later-product examples in the cited FAQ do not extend scope.

primary_citations.passage:
Push them to non-Ocean lands (as part of the same action). If the Push
also
fails somehow (perhaps due to Isolate), the pieces will be left in an illegal state and
cleaned up to the nearest land
(.7w4gdtl)
after all triggered actions complete – human pieces cannot remain in the Ocean between "action trees" (a primary action and all other actions following from it). Regardless, Ocean's Hungry Grasp does not get Energy for them.

The fact that the Push is part of the triggered action means that it can trigger further actions – e.g., "Melt Earth Into Quicksand" or "Call to Guard" in the land Pushed to – which cleaning up illegally placed pieces does not do.

Pieces representing humans
(Dahan / Invaders) are
cleaned up
to the closest legal land — this is not considered a move, is not an action, and does not trigger anything, it is simply a correction of the game state. This happens only once you are not in the middle of an action, and there are no pending triggered actions (i.e., after each action tree), just before checking for victory/defeat.

If the nearest legal land is unclear, use your best judgment, based on physical distance if necessary. If there is literally no legal land to put the pieces in, return them to the supply; this is still considered
cleaning up
(not an action, not a move/remove/destroy, does not trigger anything).

changes.current_text:
Use the named operation to determine what happens to the piece:

| Instruction | Effect on the piece |
| --- | --- |
| **Damage** | Mark Damage; reaching Health destroys the piece immediately. |
| **Destroy** | Return the specified piece to supply regardless of Health or marked Damage. |
| **Remove** | Take the specified piece off the board without a Damage-to-Health test. |
| **Replace** | Remove the original piece and put the specified new piece in its place, retaining marked Damage. |

changes.prior_text: - **Drowning:** Ocean's rule Drowns Invaders/Dahan **after** they move into the Ocean on a board with Ocean's Presence; Ocean need not have a disk in the Ocean itself. Drown destroys: Town/City Fear happens immediately, and drowned Invaders go on Ocean's panel. At any time, trade stored Invaders: **X printed Health worth of drowned Invaders for 1 Energy**, X = number of Spirits; ignore Health modifiers and make change. They need not be exchanged when Drowned; Ocean may exchange them between actions during a later Spirit Phase, including before paying for cards. Dahan drowning gives no Energy. For these rules, **humans** means all Invaders (Explorers, Towns and Cities) and Dahan. Ordinary destruction, including thematically watery Powers, is not Drowning unless specified. If Ocean loses all Presence on that board mid-action, Ocean In Play lasts through the action tree; afterward non-human pieces left there remain physically but out of play until it returns. Humans cannot stay there between action trees: if Drowning fails, Push survivors to non-Ocean lands within that action. This is an actual Push and can trigger applicable movement effects, unlike later cleanup. Failed Drowning yields no Energy. **After the primary action and all triggered actions finish**, remaining illegal humans are cleaned up to the nearest legal land. This post-action-tree correction uses the cleanup procedure below. Cleanup is not an action, move, removal or destruction and triggers nothing, and occurs before the outcome check. If no legal land exists return humans to supply as cleanup. [Core: .7w4g8qy, .9v5kbka, .7w4g8pb, .9v5ka9g, .7w4g8r4, .9v5kfqb, .9v5kfqs, .7w4gdtl]
